title: Goldenrod runtime sampling: attention kernel edge-case capture
content:
Goal:
Capture and classify non-deterministic latency spikes seen in production for attention-heavy workloads when FlashAttention and paged attention paths interact with fused op kernels. We want reproducible microbenchmarks that exercise realistic request shape variance and KV cache churn so we can (a) identify root causes, (b) propose short-term mitigations for Dedicated, and (c) propose runtime heuristics to avoid these edge cases without regressing throughput.

Background / symptom summary:
- Several customer tenants reported intermittent 95th/99th percentile token latency spikes (5–15% increase) on A100 fleets during mixed short/long prompt workloads. Spikes correlate with periods of high small-batch burstiness (many single-request, short prompts) interleaved with large streaming requests.
- Alerts surfaced around 2024-04-28 after a change to fused-kernel scheduling (PR #482). Initial revert reduced but did not fully eliminate the spikes.

Hypotheses (short):
1) Cache-line / L2 thrash when fused-op kernel selection changes rapidly between small and large seq_len, causing unpredictable memory pressure and increased kernel launch overhead.
2) Paged-attention prefetch window misprediction (prefetch depth tuned for steady long sequences) leads to repeated page faults / memory copies when sequence lengths bounce.
3) Kernel fusion microbenchmarks favor fused path for latency at mid-range seq_len but suffer throughput collapse at extreme variance due to inefficient coalescing.
4) Scheduler backpressure incorrectly coalesces different prompt shapes and causes longer queues for fused kernels.

Environment and toolchain used for tests:
- Serving runtime branch: attn-sampling-goldenrod (feature branch)
- CUDA: 12.1, cuDNN 9.x, NCCL 2.18
- GPUs: NVIDIA A100-SXM4 40GB (primary), test H100 runs for cross-checks
- FlashAttention upstream: flash-attn v2.1 with local patches from PR #482
- Measurement tools: nvprof / Nsight Systems for traces, CUPTI for hardware counters, binary tracer (lightweight) to capture kernel selection events, perf for CPU-side blocking, and the in-house latency-telemetry agent to gather p50/p95/p99.

Test matrix (representative; each cell is a 3-run median):
- Sequence lengths: constant 16, 32, 128, 512, 1024, mixed random in [8,1024]
- Batch sizes: 1, 2, 8, 16
- KV cache patterns: cold (no cache), warm (single session cache), churn (50% of requests invalidate or switch session)
- Workload mixes: steady-long (mostly >512), steady-short (mostly <=32), bursty-mixed (short and long interleaved at 10–30ms intervals)
- Kernel variants toggled: fused ops enabled/disabled, flashattention enabled/disabled, paged-prefetch depth: 0/8/32

Representative results summary:
- Steady-long: FlashAttention path gives best throughput and stable p95. No spikes.
  - 512/bs=8: throughput 22k tokens/s, p95 24ms
- Steady-short: fused-ops + small-batch coalescing shows best p50 but p95 is sensitive to batch coalescer heuristics (p95 18–40ms depending on coalescing window)
  - 32/bs=1 (coalescing on): throughput 6.8k tokens/s, p95 36ms
- Bursty-mixed (the problematic case): when fused-op selection toggles between small and large shapes within ~5–20ms, we observe repeated 95th percentile spikes of 7–12% and occasional 99th spikes up to 30%.
  - mixed/bs variable: baseline throughput 14k tokens/s, observed p95 jump to +9% vs non-bursty baseline.
- Paged prefetch misconfiguration: prefetch_depth=32 reduces paging overhead for steady-long, but for mixed workloads increases CPU -> GPU memcpy contention and contributes to tail latency increases of ~5% in p95 for small requests.

Deep observations from traces / counters:
- Kernel launch traces show frequent short-lived kernels (tens of microseconds) followed by large kernels. Overhead dominated by increased host-side scheduling and memory copies when kernel footprints change.
- L2 miss rate and DRAM read bandwidth spikes align with p95 spikes during mixed runs. This supports the L2 thrash hypothesis.
- CUPTI counters show increased SM stalls waiting on memory in fused-op kernels when a preceding small-kernel sequence ran on the same SMs previously, suggesting poor cache reuse between kernel variants.
- Nsight callstacks indicate the runtime sometimes issues fused-kernel launches with arguments that force fallback copies (alignment/padding mismatch) causing extra memcpy and kernel launch synchronization. This occurs more often with paged attention and when kv-cache blocks are partially filled.

Short-term mitigations (low-risk, fast to try):
- Add heuristic: if incoming request shapes show high variance in last N=128 requests, prefer stable non-fused kernel path for the next M=64 requests to let caches converge. This is a conservative fallback that improves p95 on mixed runs by ~6% in our test harness.
- Tune prefetch_depth dynamically: reduce depth when small-request ratio > 30% to avoid unnecessary memcopies.
- Prevent immediate kernel variant churn by adding a short hysteresis window (e.g., 2–4 scheduling cycles) before switching fusion strategy for a device/SM group.

Medium-term fixes (requires testing/signoff):
- Adjust fused-kernel launch parameters: ensure alignment/padding is normalized across small/large sequences to minimize fallback memcpy cases. This requires coordination with flash-attn tiled layout code.
- Introduce KV-cache session grouping at the runtime to schedule requests with similar sequence length/kv layout to the same worker (soft affinity). This lowers cross-kernel cache pollution at the cost of potential scheduling imbalance.
- Explore a lightweight kernel that handles small variable seq_len shapes efficiently (a smaller fused variant optimized for <64 seq_len) to reduce switching to non-fused path.

Long-term ideas:
- Add an adaptive sampler in the control plane that automatically nudges model routing to the best kernel variant per tenant workload profile and provides a runtime signal for Dedicated customers to opt-in for low-tail policies.
- Work with FlashAttention maintainers to add an optional cache-friendly launch mode that reuses padding/alignment state across consecutive launches.

Repro artifacts and commands (short notes):
- Local harness: scripts/bench/run_mixed_attack.sh --seq-dist=zipf --mix=burst:short-long --runs=3
- Kernel trace capture: scripts/traces/capture_nsight.sh --duration=60s --filter="flash*|fused*"
- Perf counter sample: python tools/collect_cupti.py --gpus 0 --counters SM__STALL --out out/

Known linked tickets / PRs:
- JIRA-ENG-3317: "p95 spikes after fused-scheduler change" (root ticket)
- GH PR #482: fused scheduler change (partial revert tested)
- GH issue #599: flash-attn alignment fallback behavior

Open questions / TODOs:
- Verify behavior on heterogeneous clusters (A100 + H100 mix) — H100 microarchitectural differences might change caches/warps behavior.
- Quantify cost of session grouping tradeoff (throughput vs tail) with a 2-week canary on a small Dedicated ring.
- Confirm whether backend allocator behavior (cudaMallocCaching) contributes to transient alignment differences; try forcing pool allocator off for a run.

Meeting notes (sync 2024-06-02):
- Decided to roll out the heuristic fallback (variance detector + non-fused path) to canary fleet for 72h.
- Marco to implement dynamic prefetch toggling and add metrics for prefetch-induced memcpy time.
- Priya to run H100 cross-checks and test allocator toggles.
- Jonah to open a small PR to normalize alignment before kernel launches and test microbench regression.

Appendix: quick checklist for reproducer run:
- Ensure driver 535.x installed and docker image compiled with same CUDA/flash-attn build.
- Run mixed harness with seed=42 to reproduce burst pattern.
- Capture Nsight trace and CUPTI counters, then compare p95 timeline to kernel selection timeline.

Notes to self: capture a short flamegraph for the p95 spike region and annotate with kernel names; include a short GIF in the follow-up Deck for the infra/ops review.
